text: Random forests provide an out-of-bag (OOB) error estimate that functions as a built-in form of cross-validation, without requiring a separate held-out validation set.
explanation: This is true: because each tree is trained on a bootstrap sample, the data points excluded from that sample ('out-of-bag') can be used to estimate generalization error, giving random forests a built-in cross-validation mechanism, as stated explicitly in the chapter.
